fixture.generation: H1 root; 1000 H2 sections each with paragraph, list item and nested list item

attribution.host: PID 75445 executable confirms Typora; host measurements include all open windows.
attribution.largeDocumentCandidate: PID 76554 WebContent started at 22:23:31, later than the two existing WebContent processes. Selected as the new document candidate based on launch timing and parent-agent report that large.md was just opened. Window-to-PID attachment is not independently proven.
attribution.backgroundControls: PIDs 75451/75452 were already running since 22:22:08/09 and are recorded separately as controls, not merged with the large-document candidate.
attribution.sharedCandidates: GPU 75448 and Networking 75453 started with Typora and may serve several windows.
attribution.excluded: Networking PID 3639 predates the current Typora launch by over one day.

units.cpuPercent: macOS ps %cpu; percentage of one CPU, scheduler-averaged rather than exact five-second interval utilization.
units.rssKiB: macOS ps resident set size in KiB; includes mapped/shared pages; not JS heap.

activity.description: First expansion followed by five collapse/expand cycles; final state expanded. Parent leaves the large window idle throughout the follow-up sampling.
activity.timingMeaning: Includes computer-use and accessibility-tree traversal overhead; not pure render latency.

limitations: Finite 60-second sampling complements resource lifecycle checks; it is not proof of leak-free operation.
macOS XPC processes report PPID 1. Large-document association is a launch-timing candidate, not a verified parent-child or window-to-PID mapping.
Background WebContent processes are shown separately; process memory is never summed as exclusive large-document memory.
Host/GPU/Networking may include all open windows; ps CPU is averaged and is not isolated plugin cost.
RSS fluctuates with GC, mapped pages and OS residency.
Computer-use accessibility/screenshot collection runs during the actions and may contribute to host/WebKit CPU and memory. This sampler cannot separate that overhead from plugin rendering.

summary.role: Typora host shared by all windows

observations: The 60-second window ended while the parent operation sequence was still being reported; idle recovery is not established by these samples.
New WebContent candidate PID 76554 reached 105.2% ps CPU and 892.062 MiB RSS. The final sample remained at 49.3% CPU and 892.062 MiB RSS.
Two older WebContent controls and shared GPU/network candidates remain separate; no aggregate is attributed solely to the large document.

This run demonstrates substantial host-side load for the exercised large-document workflow. Follow-up idle observation and action timing are needed to distinguish active workload from retained resources.
Idle follow-up is recorded separately with the same PID; the expanded mind map remains allocated, so idle RSS is not equivalent to a closed-map baseline.

idleFollowUp.role: Same large-document WebContent candidate as active sampling
idleFollowUp.activity: Large document stays expanded; parent reports no further manipulation during this segment.
idleFollowUp.interpretation: Same PID and process start identity stayed present. Across 13 idle samples CPU was 0–0.2%; RSS fell from 266.562 to 31.672 MiB, after the active-period observed maximum of 892.062 MiB. This interval demonstrates resource release after this workload; finite ps samples do not establish leak absence. RSS may also change with OS memory reclamation; PID-to-window attribution remains temporal.

computerUse.latencyMeaning: Includes CUA action and accessibility traversal; not isolated map rendering time
